candidates: When interpolating user-provided or parser-derived strings into SVG attribute values that use `url(...)` syntax (e.g. marker-start, marker-end), validate the input against an explicit allowlist (see `arrowTypesMap` in `dagre-wrapper/edgeMarker.ts`) and return early without calling `.attr()` for any unrecognized value. Do not construct the attribute string from an unvalidated input — a value containing `)` or a full URL can corrupt the `url(...)` syntax or inject a malicious reference.

When writing tests for functions that accept arbitrary strings and produce SVG or HTML attribute values, include at least one test case with a syntactically invalid input and one with a potentially malicious string (e.g. containing `)`, embedded URLs, or CSS injection attempts) to verify that the allowlist/sanitization check rejects them and leaves the element's attributes unchanged.
